audit_scope: initial primary-and-independent theory reconstruction before prototype

sources.citation: Ross PJ (2003), Modeling Soil Water and Solute Transport—Fast, Simplified Numerical Solutions, Agronomy Journal 95(6):1352-1361
source_bound_findings: method is a fast solution of the Richards equation rather than a bucket water balance
Brooks-Corey hydraulic functions were used in the original formulation
water content is the dependent variable in unsaturated regions and pressure head in saturated regions
central time weighting is used in unsaturated conditions and fully implicit weighting in saturated conditions
water flux uses matric flux potential plus a spatial weighting of the gravity component
soil-property interfaces are treated by equating fluxes to and from the interface
the reported benchmark included rainfall, ponding, evaporation and drainage over 400 h

sources.citation: Crevoisier D, Chanzy A, Voltz M (2009), Evaluation of the Ross fast solution of Richards' equation in unfavourable conditions for standard finite element methods, Advances in Water Resources 32(6):936-947
source_bound_findings: explicitly evaluates the non-iterative Ross method against HYDRUS-1D
explicitly targets conditions difficult for standard numerical methods
generalises Kirchhoff-potential evaluation numerically to hydraulic functions beyond the original Brooks-Corey case
demonstrates the generalisation with modified van Genuchten-Mualem hydraulic functions
reports Ross-method runtime between 1.25 and 14 times faster than HYDRUS-1D across its tested scenarios
reports improved robustness and a favourable speed/accuracy compromise particularly on coarse grids
sources.important_limit: The paper's tested modified VGM representation is not evidence that every SWAP hydraulic family is automatically admissible. The SWAP catalog remains a separate Gate C qualification.

sources.citation: Ross PJ (2011), Numerical Solution of the Continuity Equation for Soil Water Flow Using Precomputed Steady-State Fluxes, Vadose Zone Journal
source_bound_findings: identifies Ross 2006 Fast solution of Richards' equation for flexible soil hydraulic property descriptions as an intermediate source
uses a precomputed-steady-flux formulation that must be kept distinct from the exact 2003 algorithm until reconstructed

algorithmic_risk_register.reason: Crevoisier's demonstrated extension uses modified VGM specifically avoiding severe near-saturation nonlinearity; standard and other SWAP conductivity families require separate qualification
the fast method obtains non-iterative behaviour through a simplified linearised flux/update structure; structural bias must be measured, not hidden by aggregate errors
equating fluxes at heterogeneous interfaces can require bounded local inversion/root work even without a global Newton solve
general hydraulics may need numerical or tabulated Kirchhoff/MFP evaluation; production cost must be bounded and preferably shared/precomputed

initial_position.reason: The literature supports a credible non-iterative Richards-derived route and shows that Brooks-Corey is not a fundamental blocker, but exact SWAP-catalog hydraulics, conservation, coupling and bounded local work remain unqualified.

next_actions: reconstruct the exact Ross 2003 discrete update and identify every approximation
obtain and inspect Ross 2006 flexible-hydraulics report if publicly accessible
derive a hydraulic-provider contract using SWAP K(h), theta(h), inverse h(theta) and MFP/Kirchhoff potential without changing physics
prove a per-step finite-volume mass ledger before a full profile prototype
define a bounded local heterogeneous-interface solve with explicit failure semantics
only then implement an isolated reference harness
